description: VECTOR_TRUNC and its alias VECTOR_TRUNCATE - every expectation measured on a real Snowflake account. It keeps the FIRST n dimensions and narrows the STATIC type accordingly, the element type is PRESERVED so an INT vector does not become FLOAT, n = 0 is the empty vector and n = the full dimension is the unchanged vector. An integral DECIMAL dimension such as 2.0 is accepted. A typed NULL vector gives SQL NULL. A dimension beyond the vector names both numbers: 'Requested truncation dimension 4 for VECTOR_TRUNC should be less than or equal to the dimension of the provided vector (3).' - and the alias names ITSELF in that sentence. The dimension must be a CONSTANT: a column reference, an arithmetic expression, a non-integral literal and NULL are all '... needs to be constant', each quoting what it found - live numbers the argument 2 for a column and 1 for an expression, so the steps match the quoted part. A non-vector first argument is the ordinary argument-type list. Converted 1:1 from functions/vector/VectorTruncTest (now retired); every vector is read as a bare cell, as recorded in functions-vector-avg. The Java's assertRejected only asserted that something threw, so the rejection cases pin live's messages - except a negated dimension, which the account answers with an internal error, so that step only requires a refusal.
